If the UI was complete, a guide wouldn't be necessary. But there are so many features that you can only really figure out after spending dozens of hours playing this game. And since some mechanics don't work, you're never even sure if what you learn will change in the near future as the devs process bug reports and feedback. Don't get me wrong, it's fun so far. But I wouldn't buy this game for at least another year.

I do not mind the leaner aspect of the game, but some stuff like not being able to queue science tree, or that i have to click hundred times to make an trade icon move to a city or trade routes that aren't working properly, or the fact that you still cant attack with your army for some odd reason, and without explanation - everything is grayed out, here would be a welcome time for some tips in-game. Crisis scenarios with random people starving or being ill and you having to get less gold from an altar is far fetched logic, but ok. So all-in-all ill try to complete one scenario but I doubt if Ill ever play this again. I would advise ppl not to spend so much cash on this game till maybe after feedback from the community they patch and revamp major problems. Now more hours in, started war, ofcourse. For example, one of the core mechanics of the exploration age, generating treasure fleets, necessary to pursue a commerce victory, requires that you access at least 5 copies of exotic resources, not available on your home continent. This meant that I would have to engage in war with another fully developed civ on the other side of the ocean and conquer (and keep) one of their cities - to be able to just START generating treasure fleets.

Verdict: Civilization VII attempts to shake up the formula, but not always successfully. Some new mechanics are interesting, but the game loses part of its uniqueness and accessibility. Civilization VII introduces significant changes compared to its predecessors, offering enjoyable combat mechanics, city-building, and overall gameplay. However, the game’s age system feels too drastic, often disrupting progress rather than fostering a natural sense of advancement. The age transitions frequently reset key aspects of the game, including the economy, trade routes, and sometimes even adjacency bonuses, which can throw off carefully planned strategies. In some cases, the transition may even result in the deletion of army units, further hampering progress. Because each age feels so distinct, I often found myself fixing my economy and production rather than progressing smoothly through history. A more balanced approach—where only dark ages impose severe penalties—would help maintain a sense of continuity. Additionally, some civilizations feel unbalanced. For example, the Normans’ basic soldiers are mere swordsmen, while the Spanish enter the Middle Ages equipped with muskets, creating an unfair advantage. Hopefully, future updates will address these issues, refining both the age transitions and civilization balancing for a smoother and more strategic game play experience. Overall the game is enjoyable and music is amazing I hope the age transitions are improved.

Despite its promising visuals, Civilization VII feels like a step backward for the series. As a veteran with 2000+ hours in Civ V and VI and experience since Civ II, the biggest issues are the awkward UI and poor information display. While cities look great, it's hard to tell what you've built, and the map lacks readability. The new commander system adds interesting tactical depth, but removing unit skill levels makes individual combat feel meaningless and less fun. The gutting of resource strategy mechanics removes another layer of meaningful decision-making that made previous games engaging. Limiting settlers through the happiness system feels like artificial restriction rather than good game design, and the removal of builders reduces player agency. Basic features like automated exploration are mysteriously absent, making the game more tedious than fun. Even after several hours, it's still unclear how many units you can support or why AI civs suddenly plant cities between your territories. Between the simplified resource system and other streamlined mechanics, it's hard to find the engaging strategic elements that made previous titles so addictive. While the game might improve with patches, this feels like more than a few balance tweaks away from greatness. The simplified systems and clunky interface suggest a troubling shift toward console gaming conventions - a cardinal sin for a franchise that helped define PC strategy gaming. The Founder's Edition currently feels like a waste if money.

I have thousands of hours into the history of the Civ franchise and love it. I purchased the founders pack hoping that all the hype was worth and new Civ game. Civ 7 is a very different from what Civ players love and enjoy about the game. This rendition is broken into 3 mini games (ages) that loosely hold continuity together. The 3 ages have way to much history crammed into a sub age, but is managable. You need to play in marathon to enjoy all of it. There are some new features introduce that are a good addition to the game but the split of three ages breaks the immersion of being a civilization playable through time. You have to choose a different culture each age. There are many missing features that need to be put back into the game to make it more playable. They took out auto-explore, unit UI control, limited tech trees. A very awkward town to city sub system that you have to invest heavily into to gain any resources or usability from expanding from more than your one city. Then you have all of that ripped away at the abrupt end of an age. At that transition you lose cities, (turn back into towns) which you have to buy and then build up again to be useful. All but a few units are destroyed and those few are put in there place at that age level. You have to start over in the new age and re-chose how you are going to play in the segmented mini games. Many of the new features seem to have been copied from Humankind in how the civics and policies come into play and many more added in to pop up at certain tech levels. The map sizes are way to small to play any decent game, tiny, small, and standard. Standard is a very cramped map. The map seeds usually place most of the AI Civs within a city area away from you. Not to mention all of the hostile (barbarian) city states which you have to dump tons of resources into just for a hope that they wont attack you constantly. The city states are able to pump out units every turn and wage war on you as the AI Civs do the same. Attempting to survive the onslaught of the AI gang-banging you while trying to complete quests inside of each mini game is a miracle. Even though if by some chance you might be crushing the globe under your foot, to then lose at the abrupt end of the age if you haven't completed enough quests. It is a steep learning curve and have to micro mange every detail to achieve success. I do recommend playing marathon mode with all tutorials on for the first play through.

In general, the game looks great, and a lot of the basic game play is fine, but certain areas of game play still seem half-baked and unbalanced. In particular, NPC leaders seems insufficiently differentiated in their strategies. It is as if the AI has been trained to make them all hyper-aggressive, and their approaches are weirdly synchronized. It feels more like playing against one AI that wields multiple leaders, rather than seeing different personalities, tendencies, and approaches, the way Civ VI tends to play. Diplomacy is a constant whack-a-mole to try to reduce hostility from other leaders, even when they have no principled reason to be hostile. Unlike Civ VI, past transgressions and favors don't seem to age out, so the other leaders stay angry about things that happened a 1000 years before. Other intermediate goals also seem to trigger the AI leaders to all behave the same: during the Age of Exploration, once religions get established, there is suddenly a bum's rush by all the leaders to send out missionaries, like your worst nightmare of a theocratic Catholic Spain in Civ VI, but it is everybody all at once. Or in the Modern Age, all the leaders suddenly create explorers, and the AI is running them all to the exact same excavation sites at the same time, so you can arrive and find a stack of a dozen explorers from 4 leaders on the same hex for one dig, and that same stack trundles around as a group to every other dig site. It is a mad rush to stay ahead of the AI playing the same strategy for every leader at the same time. The game also seems to lack some basic report screens that would make it easier to keep an overview of what your cities and towns are doing. P.S. The problem of the explore rush seems to have been addressed in the latest patch.

Honestly as someone with nearly a thousand hours into Civ5 and 150 hours into Civ6 I like the bones of this game a lot more than civ6. The mixing of Civ's is something I could take or leave, kinda liked persistent aesthetics, but also like changing things up from age to age, so that's cool I guess. For me the game's issue (and why i can't leave a positive review) is purely based off game stability and UI choices. I haven't experienced any lag issues or frame rate dips, nor any crazy sudden spikes in memory usage that i noticed happened a bit on Civ6 release date so that's nice. However the save file glitch alone makes the game quite literally unplayable as it was intended to be played, as such I wonder if it even complies with consumer laws as it's technically a broken product being sold. In addition, the endless please wait turn timer has returned, which is something I vaguely recall in Civ5 almost ten years ago when I was running it off what was essentially a dumpster lid with wires, and should not really be an issue with my current hardware which more than surpasses the recommended requirements for the game. DLC policy is neither here nor there, that's purely based on individuals opinions so I won't really comment one way or another. I did not participate in the Civ6 passes and other stuff, and i feel no obligation to here, i will however, probably pick up the expansions when they come out. I know Civ releases can be a little rough (I was a kid when civ5 came out and I remember what it was like before G&K and Brave New World came out) but this is kinda basic stuff like being able to hit the turn button, which you know, I feel should probably work on release. The UI is probably the game's biggest issue in terms of style and actual gameplay, its lifeless, sterile, and feels rushed. Having opponents diplo tabs taking up half the top right of the screen was certainly a choice, as that was an issue I had with civ6 and their little face bubbles to be honest. I will say I appreciate the idea of moving the diplo stuff from a separate tab like in civ5, but honestly I think that's probably the way to go, a simple small drop-down menu. Also using influence is a neat idea, but the whole screen needs a complete overhaul, its kinda stinky right now. the menu is confusing, not intuitive and just a little clunky.I look forward to this game being playable over the next two years, that said it was still a better launch then humankind, so I guess in the current state of the turn based civ builder market, Faraxis is still kinda limping ahead of everyone else. I don't blame anyone for holding out on the game until much later, as that is the financially wise calculation to make, I being a longtime civ fan was just curious to see what this game would look like before I pour several hundred hours into it when its actually good. Save your money for now. Also one more turn button and more map sliders would be greatly appreciated.

Dislikes/Improvement Areas: The game is not without issues. As noted, UI needs work. There a number of things that could be intuitive but are not. This ranges from un-clear explanations as to why I could not perform some action, to basics such as not being able to drag and drop resources/great works. The UI does not feel great, and I suspect this is because the game was launched with consoles in mind. I hope improvements going forward bring some more intuitive PC interaction while maintaining support for console players. I also miss the ability to select a city and see the outline of the tiles inside the boundary. This can only be done during an expansion event. There are a number of little details like that in the UI that are missing (or I have not found). Outside of UI, I did have other criticisms. I did feel slightly underwhelmed by the end victory screen. I liked seeing all the numbers and charts they had tracking progress from turn 1. This may be tricky with the ages, but I would love to see this come back. There were some bugs, as expected early in launch. I could not select 1 civ in the modern age, despite playing an exploration civ the was supposed to unlock it. That was the most obvious one. On the whole I still feel the good outweighs the bad, and would recommend.

Since I haven't finished a game yet, it's too early to say, but so far the gameplay changes solve or at least improve on major problems that have plagued all prior Civ games: there's less incentive to save-scum, and the age transitions and city vs town distinctions significantly cut down both the micromanagement that becomes increasingly tedious as more and more productive cities result in more and more (often pointless) build orders every turn. In every previous version, end games are typically boring, because the game is almost always decided 100 turns away from reaching the victory condition. I haven't finished a game of Civ 6 in years because it's so tiresome to just click through turn after turn waiting to rack up enough tourism or capture the last city or whatever. I don't know yet if Civ 7 fully solves that issue, but it looks very promising.

It should be clearly visible in the tree with the Happiness icon or at least some color code. I have played every version of Civilization including Call to Power and Alpha Centauri. Civ VI took a step back from Civ V when it first came out but Civ VI eventually carved out its own space in the Civ universe. Unfortunately, I can't see how Civ VII can replicate that. Civ VII's greatest sin is it's boring. These types of games may all be spreadsheets underneath but Civ VII feels like a spreadsheet on the surface. You don't feel like you have just built the Parthenon, you feel like you just added a statistical adjustment. The Ages kill any sense of ownership and progress. They also destroy the illusion you are creating a civilization (why do I have to be the Egyptians to become the Prussians?) A true start earth map would never work with this version. The further elimination of historical leaders in favor of virtue signalling feels like the designers forcing their values on the players (Harriet Tubman but no George Washington? Really?) Here's a tip: Sometimes a barbarian is just a barbarian. By far the greatest sin is they didn't fix the AI. The AI is terrible. AI capabilities have definitely advanced to the level where Civ VII COULD have a great AI. Unfortunately function has definitely taken a backseat to form and virtual signaling. I hope there is way for Firaxis to salvage the bones of Civ VII and rebuild it.

Civ 6 (Yes, SIX) is the pinnacle of Civ games. You have continuity, the freedom to choose your own path to victory, clear and direct objectives and goals and clear and direct methods and strategies for accomplishing those goals. Civilization 6 gave you a sense of purpose as you played, and a rewarding sense of accomplishment when you achieved any victory, big or small. Civilization 7 does a terrible job at best in these regards. Playing through a game of Civ 7 feels like mindlessly trudging through a bog of unnecessary complication. The game developers took everything good from Civ 6 and transformed it into a complex web of handcuffing flow charts and accomplishment trees. I despise how Civilization 7 pigeon holes your game play into a predetermined narrative. Just as I feel that I've established my civilization in this world, the age ends and FORCES me to abandon my civilization (nationality) and start again with a new one. And heaven forbid I should want to expedite my exploration of the world early in the game or expand my empire to a different hemisphere before the game narrative deems it is okay to do so. Civilization 7 is the first Civ game that I have played in this series in which the hours that I've played during a session feel wasted rather than enjoyed. My Civilization Saturdays will be better spent going back and enjoying Civ 6 from this point forward.

I have played Civilization since i was kid, starting with Civ 3. I loved Civ 4, with Civ 6 being my favorite. I didn't really play Civ 5 for some reason, probably will now. I have never wrote a review for any game, ever. I ordered the founders package, not to play earlier but since i love civilization franchise , I didn't want to wait for the extra DLC. I realize that games now, always have bugs or issues upon release that are eventually, patched or updated. Right now this game is complete hot garbage. I will ignore (not event mad) of the whole woke/DEI and supposedly Harriett Tubman controversy. Granted she is a relatively important American historical figure but there are more important ones, I would have preferred Fredrick Douglas if they were trying to find new historical people (good idea on trying to introduce new leaders) but some are historical figures that everyone knows for a reason. Tubman addition not a complete surprise since civ 6 went a little woke with Abraham Lincoln in Civ 6. I could be wrong but Lincoln was the only leader in civ 6 that had a negative attribute for something (plantations). I do give credit to them for trying new things by introducing new leaders. Overall, my problem is that they tried to do to much and over complicated the game with over abundant of decision making, mechanics, and systems. I played 215 turns with Roman Empire and Augustus. My specific issues and problems are listed below. First, I agree with other reviews, the UI is awful. I find it very cumbersome and not very informative on new things. Some of the new things, don't need 50 page manual to understand but maybe a little instructions of the pro and cons of the narrative events that seemingly happen for no reason. Half the fun more me was figuring it out myself. I never got passed researching the wheel in science tree, and the special Roman Civic attributes in civic tree. I was about 60 percent through the antiquity age, then age counter shot up to 99%, after AI player conquered another AI player. Then the antiquity age had one more turn before exploration age. Once in exploration age, it was a complete new science and civic tree that represented the middle ages (basically time jump and automatically researched all the science and civics, I did not research). Unless I'm wrong, to my understanding all the other AI civs also advanced in technology to catch up exploration age. Which if the case true is extremely dumb because your basically getting reward for bad strategy and penalized for good strategy. Once I choose the Normans, I couldn't finish building special Roman buildings or Roman specific techs/civics, plus half my military units disappeared (the game noted that half my units would disappear in the new age). I specifically trained more military units and sacrificed certain building for later, since Rome is militaristic. Additionally, once i reached exploration, I couldn't build any wonders from antiquity era. Also when changing to a new age you are not free to choose any new civilization, only certain ones that somewhat similar or historically accurate to one before (my choices after Rome, were Norman or Spain). I think it is an interesting idea to choose another civilization but I prefer to change leaders upon reaching a new age or the option to mix and match any leader for any civilization when the time comes. I think you should be able to choose whatever path you want. Play as Rome or America and stay that civilization then transition to a new Roman or American leader with different unique characteristic as you progress to new age or start as Rome then transition to England or France, then transition to America with either Roman leaders or new leader specific that new civilization. I also don't like the crisis and happiness aspect. I tried hard to to make good balanced decision between happiness, production, and food (as needed) but even if you make good decisions even if not the most efficient or proficient decisions, you have to choose various crisis problem to deal with as progress to the next age. My crisis was a happiness problem, despite going slow in expanding cities ( if you expand to quickly and go over your settlement limit you lose happiness). A settlement limit is dumb, if i want to produce an settle a bunch of towns and cities that should be my choice. I was making sure the happiness system was good but as I got closer to the new age, my happiness plummeted drastically, despite trying account for potential happiness problem. If your planning your cities well and progressing, why should I have a crisis, or have to choose one before moving to new age. Maybe the crisis event happen when you are not progressing and making bad decisions, like in civ 6 and you go to the dark ages or similar. In closing, a lot of good ideas but poor execution in game play because it is very restrictive. In my opinion they made to many changes, in trying to make the game bigger and over complicated it with to many decisions/systems/mechanics and DEI (not because of Harriet Tubman). The DEI concerns are specifically in the feeling that they tried to make the game to historically accurate. It is a game and a fantasy game at that. Why can't I start as America in ancient or antiquity era and go forward or bring Rome, Mayans, and etc into the modern age. The game feels like they just incorporated all the stuff I did not like about humankind. Humankind was ok, had some merits for different mechanics and ideas but in the end I stopped playing Humankind after a few months. Civ 6 had great ideas but very simple and not overly complicated, like apostle and influence by settling to close to another civilization. If they had just tweaked some of systems and mechanics instead implementing the concept of making it bigger and more complex will make it better (bigger and more complex doesn't always make things better). I highly recommend not buying this game if your a fan of civilization games from the past.

Apex Legends is a game I have played for 4 years, and I have definitely seen its ups and downs as time passed. I would personally recommend this game not just because it is fun, but because it has its own unique characteristics in comparison to other Battle Royale games like COD Warzone and Fortnite. You can certainly look up many things about this game, but I believe that it is most likely guaranteed you will find a legend in the roster that suits you best. There is also a great amount of customization in this game (Which can be very expensive if you choose to spend money on this game), comparable to the likes of the games I mentioned prior, with extra possessions like your tailored banner. The last thing I will say before I review this game critically is that it may be tough for new players, though if you research ways to get better online you will get through it. Now, since we have sung its praises with many more that I did not mention, we must now look at what apex does not get right or what it could fix to do better. Hacking is currently rampant in apex, especially in the competitive mode as you move up the ranks. This has been a problem for a very long time, possibly dating back to season 2 (when I started playing), when I was on console so at that time hacking was barely a concern or even not a concern at all, while when I switched to PC in season 3, I personally started seeing cheaters in game as soon as season 5. It also relates to the large incident that happened in ALGS recently, where 2 players (Genburten and ImperialHal) had their game hijacked, giving them esp with full hitboxes, health, and player names, along with bullet (not aim-locking) aimbot. Hacking is the only concern I will describe in this review because it has been recent, and is a genuine concern and has been for a long time. In conclusion, while apex has many great qualities I mentioned, there are some concerns that do not have to do with how the game is intended to be played. I would personally give the game an 8.9/10, because despite its shortcomings, it is unique, it can be tailored, and most of all, it is great, but its shortcomings hinder me from giving it a 9/10 (Amazing). Opinions can differ widely on how good or bad this game is depending on who you ask, so I am not expecting you to 100% believe in my opinion, and all I ask of you is that you at the very least consider it.

Every single match, no matter what lobby you go to, has cheating, and not even like 1 person, entire teams fighting each other with cheats. Soft cheats, hard cheats, you name it. They don't even try to hide it. It reminds me of Lance Armstrong's story of how he said he used drugs because everyone was using them and the only way to have fair combat was to doing them yourselves. Apex is literally in that state where people are using cheats just to be on par, can you imagine. The game has never been this bad in terms of cheating, balance, moral, player count or monetisation. Such a shame because the gameplay loop of Apex is still the best there is, it can definitely be better, but none of the other shooters feel as good, however if you can't even enjoy that anymore, there is nothing left. I doubt anyone from Respawn actually plays their own game or even cares anymore. I think the time has come for this game to be given to a different studio, one that is fresh with joy and wants to do well with Apex. A new studio should build the game from the ground up on Unreal Engine, and build internal anti cheat mechanics, and not replay on easy Anti Cheat and the like. It's the only way to combat the current state of the game. However the good news is, the core game itself is so bad now, for the first time in years, I genuinely don't feel like playing it. I actually want to thank the cheaters and devs for not caring, it's what I needed to leave for good. This game isn't good for anyone's health, even if you have a good life, this game will do everything it can to ruin it, and that's when its working well. It's been fun, had some great moments, got some mad clips, will definitely remember the good times but will also remember the lack of respect and care from both the players you encounter and the devs, and their tactics. At the end of the day this is a battle royal through and through, so from its core there is nothing super unique about the game from that aspect. However the Legends and game play keep it above the seemingly endless sea for free-2-play BR's out there on the market. Whether you enjoy shooters from a casual perspective or you enjoy a test of skill. Whether you are seeking a trio to win or go after self-glory, this game has plenty to offer.

I can say for sure that this is definitely one of my favorite battle royale games by far, in the top 3 for sure. This game was just perfect in every possible way, honestly speaking I don't even know what they could've made better. The guns, the movement, the map, the new stuff they add, just everything about Apex Legends was so good. The first time I played it was on the exact release date (Feb 4, 2019) on my PS4, and I played it with my cousin. We decided to play in groups of three so we could get some help to win since we were new to the game. Surprisingly, our first game matched us with someone who was already pretty good at the game, even though it was the first day it was ever launched. He totally carried us to victory, no joke. Me and my cousin only got like 1 kill each, and we ended up winning our first game on the first release day, which is still crazy to me. I'm grateful I got to play most of the seasons, especially the OG ones. I loved it a lot, including the Hemlock, which is one of my favorite guns in the whole game. Honestly, I can't complain except for the fact that your account isn't the same on PS4 or PS5 or any other platform you play on. I played on PS4 for a long time and had so many cool skins, battle pass stuff, and gun wraps. My account was fully maxed out until I switched to PC. Even though I used the same EA account, it took me to a new account on PC. It basically had nothing on it, like starting over again. It got me really annoyed and frustrated, but I managed to grind a bit more and almost maxed it out again. I really wish I could play this game more. Also, I don't like that there isn't a solo mode. I kinda get why, but sometimes playing with random people can be really annoying. But again, I can't complain because most games aren't as good as Apex Legends. I honestly recommend anyone to play this game, though I suggest playing it with a friend or family member, just anyone you can talk to. Overall, it's a great game and definitely beats most shooter games like Fortnite, Warzone, PUBG, and the rest. This is just my opinion and if you disagree, that's okay. I hope you find this review useful!

Imagine owning a franchise longer than the original owners and still not understanding what the actual soul of the franchise is. Started off with a bunch of potential but still fumbling it time and time again. Always one step forward, two steps back with each update. This game was a huge step in the right direction when it first released, returning to the art style and gameplay of the older games with a modern take. The weapon sandbox though is abysmal. Why do Halo 2 and 3 have a more diverse sandbox than this game while being almost two decades old? Weapons were fun and interchangeable, what happened? Now, everything is so stiff. The few weapons from the old games that have been brought in feel good but what the hell were 343 thinking with some of the Banished weapons? Fighting mainly Brutes. No Brute Shot. No Brute Plasma Rifle. No Mauler (a BRUTE weapon). but it's okay because we got the "MaNgLer" and the "SkEwEr." So many missing guns that help fill the gaps and make the game actually fun. But no. Instead adding in some BS Fuel Rod Cannon that's just a reskin of the default rocket launcher. The vehicles are just.... why...? Ghost is clunky like the Halo: CE one, and not in a fun nostalgic way. Chopper handles like trying to stand on an oiled up beach ball in the middle of the ocean. Might as well not even use the Banshee. And not only that but having the worst standalone story of the entire franchise that goes absolutely nowhere. By the time you watched the first cutscene, you find out everything interesting has already happened off screen. You get to be Chief, meandering about a Halo ring with no stakes or sense of what the hell is going on. No real prior links or characters to reel you in. Just get to listen to a whiny pilot cry and give him a pat on the shoulder when he's sad. I really wanted this game to succeed. Had hope it'd take off at some point but the only thing it actually has going for it are nice graphics and a good Forge mode, that it took years to release. I can't find any reason to play this game over the old Bungie games. It's just soulless and wants your money. Especially moreso now since they have to have FOMO for the Battle Passes. That was never supposed to be a thing. Hell. No one asked for a Free-to-Play Halo. Don't even bother with this. For a LIVE service game, expect to get one weapon added a year and maybe one singular vehicle during the game's lifespan. But don't worry. In the meantime, you can throw $20 for a singular armor set.... Get real.

They ambush the Infinity and cause it to crash land on the surface of the ring. Can you survive the Banished onslaught? Discover the secrets of Zeta Halo? Unlock powerful new subvariants of weapons both new and old to the series by defeating wanted criminals of the UNSC? Rebuild the human forces of the fallen Infinity. Retake the ring from Banished control. And finally, discover what really happened on Zeta during the six months you were floating in space after being tossed out of an airlock by a new nemesis.

Long time Civilization game player here. Since Civ I, Age of Empire, as well as Space 4x genre which I have always though of as Civ in Space. Humankind is EXCELLENT. Every bit as good as Civ VI, and better in many ways. The transition between cultures is very fun, and truly allow you to shore up your strategy as the game unfolds. Victory Points are forever, and the in this game they are achievement stars - you always know what you could be doing to get closer to winning. This is very well done, and a feature that ever player of the genre will admire. Combat is tactical, or automated. I find I can usually do a little better than the automation, so when it really matters I will control combat. The only cons: unfortunately, like Civ... it can get a bit boring near the end of the game, when you are clearly crushing everyone - but the conditions must be met.

Instead, the rotating cast of cultures means everyone feels much the same, everyone changes quickly, and you don't have the same investment in the game. Do I care that Red and Blue are at war? I probably should, but only if it means one has more "Fame", whatever the heck that is. There's nothing quite like the feeling of teching up only to run into a roadblock where you can't get enough Fame stars for the next era, and instead watch Green run away with the game because they took three cities instead of two. It could have been really fun to see Zhou go into Ming or Han, then Edo or Viet, then China or Japan, but no; everyone can go anywhere, and often it feels like the game was decided a hundred meaningless moves ago. At least in Civ I have an actual character to yell at when they take my city location instead of some knock-off Mii.

In conclusion, while Civilization 6 has long been a staple in the strategy gaming community, Humankind emerges as a worthy contender, if not a superior successor. With its innovative mechanics, diverse civilizations, stunning visuals, and refined AI, Humankind sets a new standard for the genre. Whether you're a seasoned strategist or a newcomer to the genre, Humankind offers an unparalleled experience that's sure to keep you coming back for more. Amplitude Studios has truly outdone themselves with this masterpiece, and I eagerly anticipate what the future holds for this incredible game.

For fans of 4x nation builder games, this turn-based strategy game is a refreshing take. The mechanics of victory and progress are distinct enough to allow for genuinely different approaches to achieve your victory - first, while still building on a lot of the standard resource and opportunity cost principles. The expansions all add distinct and engaging optional additions to a well-developed game, adding possible complexities and variables, that force new strategies and approaches as the game progresses. While some mechanics will require you to grow familiar, and they still haven't bothered to make the AI actually engaging to play against, the game is quite fun and a great addition to the 4x genre.

A somewhat fresh take on the 4X strategy genre. You build a civilization that evolves by blending different cultures across eras. So, in the Stone Age you're Egyptians, in the Bronze Age you switch to Hettites, and in the Dark Age you roll with Teutons, and so on. This mix-and-match approach keeps gameplay quite exciting and your strategy adaptable as each nation comes with certain bonuses and spceial troops. City-building is also deep, with cities that can grow by absorbing adjacent territories. Battles are round-based tactical. Diplomacy allows to respond to your actions with a grievance system. Overall, a great game if you enjoy city and empire builder games.

Constant freezing, computer blue-screens, forced easy anticheat (Which I believe is causing many crashes etc) for "online" features such as mycareer, even if you have no intention to play anything online. Menus taking way too long to load for such simple features (even with strong computer hardware). Poor simulation accuracy in many instances, rigged ai (to compensate for poor ai), many features working only about 15% of the time on a good day (such as NBA start today MyLeague, downloading custom team designs etc...), still terrible support for key board key-binds (where things like editing player tendencies are such necessary changes to mimic realistic simulation, you'd think having a keyboard would mean you could easily type the values, or use pg up and pg down keys etc to quickly alter values, same thing goes for negotiating player/coach contracts). Coaching system still is terrible and has no consistent tangible value. Alterations to offensive/defensive formations on the time out screen are dependent on which team calls timeout for some reason still, ie offensive changes can only be made you take a timeout on offense, defensive changes can only be made on the whim of CPU taking a timeout at a time you wish to make adjustments (this issue has been present for at least 2 games now). AI gets every foul call where you get seemingly none, defenders on the players team's speed gets throttled as soon as the game decides its time a cpu player to get a bucket. CPU will get perfect shot and dribble animations to completely cancel out player defense, where player animations get the opposite. Shot meter and timing changes are awful and I've switched to playing purely real player %. Player AI has no concept of off-ball movement or spacing on offense, which makes it really easy for CPU to defend your whole team even when conceptually at disadvantage, meanwhile player AI on defense has no concept of proper help defense strategy and will entirely ignore manual coaching changes made to try and fix the issue. Modern offensive strategies such as guards screening for other guards is almost impossible to configure to happen in real life (as the only possible screeners are C/PFs when manually calling for screen). When creating a new MyLeague, they forgot to include the option to import settings, so you have to import your custom settings AFTER the season has already started which is really annoying. Real life strategies often are almost entirely impossible to replicate in game because the extreme balancing changes that have been done to prevent PvP cheesing (such as deep 3's, DHO's, cutting). Switching AI is INCREDIBLY slow and they somehow made it worse than previous gen ai. Historical rosters are a joke. Essentially no creativity available for offensive or defensive schemes. Every game and team composition feels the exact same without wildly altering player sliders(which are very difficult to understand in many cases). Player progression and Training has been entirely gutted. Allstar festivities still suck and are boring. Post season things are still flat and meaningless. Player farewell-tours are unnoticeable. Every aspect, from game stability, in-game gameplay, season simulation, player customization of team strategy, and every other facet of this game, are somehow worse than ever. Absolute pathetic excuse of a leadership team - the programmers, animators, and everyone else deserves better than these rushed corporate BS releases. Please will another company step in to compete with the fools in charge of 2k.

Generally a pretty solid 2k game, and they actually updated PC to use the next-gen (current at this point?) version of the game which is greatly appreciated. There were/are a few bugs that could be pretty frustrating such as hearing the opponents in rec which led to griefing (patched), and the ever prevalent issue of the shot meter randomly resetting between games. However, as long as you have just a slight degree of vigilance, that's fairly manageable. My biggest issues are with some parts of the structure of the game itself, that is, the rep system and the cost of builds. For me to even hit Vet II for my reputation, I was well over 1000 hours into the game, and that really just isn't attainable for a vast number of player. I understand gatekeeping some of the higher ranks and associated rewards to players who are committed to the game, but it also makes it that much harder to play literally anything else when you need to have such a crazy high time commitment to reach what appears to be just past the middle of the rep rank system. As for the builds in this game, there is a lot of freedom in terms of what you can do, and cap breakers make that even more true. To some extent, you have a much greater ability to make a true superstar than you have had for probably the past decade of 2k games. However, the prevalence of things like cap breakers and more diverse builds also make it a lot easier to fall into the trap of wanting many MyCareer builds. Having many options to choose from may seem nice, but upgrading each of them costs about 100$ to max out, and getting the VC to upgrade players without purchasing it is unsustainable. Regardless, the biggest concern I had when I switched from console to PC 2K was whether or not there would be a large enough playerbase to consistently find games and also the prevalence of hacking in the community. I can happily say that hackers have been few and far between in this rendition, and while they of course do exist, I only run into them online in probably 1/20-1/25 games. At the beginning of the year, this was probably closer to 1/100-1/150, but I have been okay with this ratio anyways. As for the concerns with the playerbase, I have also been happily surprised. I am usually able to get into a game in just a few minutes, with notable exceptions being when it's extremely late at night/earlier morning (2 AM - 8:30 am ish). The park usually has one lobby still active and running during this time (It's always Rise), but as a Rec player, I know that I can't find games in that window. As a whole, the game is a fairly solid 2k and definitely the one that I have put the most hours into, but it has a few flaws in terms of 2k being fairly money hungry (which is nothing new) and some minor flaws related to it being the PC version of a primarily console game community.

Modes like MyPlayer and MyTeam are quite literally unplayable without spending money and every year VC grows in inflation. The seasons system is predatory and further forces you to have to either spend money or invest an unreasonable amount of time in order to keep up with the folks that pay. The gameplay has always been solid so I have no complaints in that department. MyNBA/Eras is the mode I have been playing the most for the past few years but since that mode doesn't make 2K any money they invest little energy to improve and refine the mode as much as they could. Overall I have only been buying the game when it is substantially discounted for the reasons stated above. I hope for the future sake of the franchise that they find a compromise between making their stockholders money and delivering a solid product to their consumers. For the most part, NBA 2K25 was the right time for PC players to get back into NBA 2K. The game runs on Next Gen already, meaning if I got it right, a PC player can now play online with a console player. However, I have one huge bit of negative feedback about the game. I've been playing for quite some time now and I've noticed that every so often, the game falls into these periods where a glitch comes out. I call them boomerang passing. The pass doesn't get completed from the passer to the intended receiver. Instead, the ball boomerangs back to the passer. Because of this, the game becomes mostly unplayable. Inbound passes become out of bounds violations, the shot clock runs out because the NPC can't pass it back to the PC. And some shots go wild because they boomerang back to the shooter. Lately I've noticed this glitch come up whenever the game gets an update - the end of a Season, holiday updates (Halloween and, now, Christmas). I've asked a friend who has the game on a console and he hasn't experienced anything like what I described. I hope 2K is able to address this, or at least provide a solution for us non-console gamers. Arguably the best season of OW2 was the first, as they removed stuns, but they choose to give the new characters hinders and knock backs abilities. Overall, we are taking a big step in the right direction every update, which gives me hope for OW2.

Some supports are so weak in fact that they rarely get a kill (mainly mercy whos only damage is a little pistol). If you look it up Blizzard has talked about how they score this and a ranked games and they have a very clunky scoring system. If you say anything that could be perceived as offensive in chat, you will get a point on your account towards silence, suspension, or ban. Reporting for anything but cheating and abusive chat will do literally nothing. People who’ve spent countless hours and money on this game can be spam reported by literally any group of malicious actors and get their account banned for anything(pfp, name, hero pick, play style, you name it). It’s not the report that matters, it’s the number of reports that matter. So long as someone paints a target on your back, you can lose access to the game even if you had your chat turned off! It’s so wild to me. Anyways, I feel like spending money on the game just to get your account banned from playing into the same petty 5-stack multiple games in a row(because there aren’t many players on at the time/they’re bleeding players) isn’t cool. It would be nice if they could reinstate all accounts that got banned for chat and simply silence them/give them endorsement level 0. Alright look, despite what everyone is going to review about this game, at its core, and as a whole, I still believe this game has value. It will never be what it once was 10 years ago. Fresh, revolutionary, and unique. The game space has changed and the transition from Overwatch 1 to Overwatch 2 may have been unnecessary all together, but in a way it, was a necessary evil for the future of the game. How Blizzard went about it was horrible including the lies and deceit in regard to the PvE content. The balance team has absolutely no idea what they are doing or have been doing for the past 7 years (both new AND old teams). However, after all is said and done, this game gets frequent updates (100x more than Overwatch 1 ever did) at it's whole, and at its core, will still be just a fun casual game to get on and play for a bit either by yourself or with friends. Anybody looking for a hard-hitting competitive game to grind and climb in should definitely look elsewhere. If you are looking for a fun casual experience, then Overwatch 2 will not disappoint you. To reiterate, this game is for casual gamers looking for a fun time getting to play with unique hero characters and learn the ins and outs of team play with some moments of of solo carry potential to spice things up. For those looking for die hard competitive game to grind hours and hours on, the horrible balance (especially as you climb the ranks) preventing you from potentially playing your newly discovered favorite heroes will, and at times horrible 50/50 matchmaking will drive you away.

The game is great in my opinion but has too many flaws within the game that too many people have commented on already. The biggest fumble this game contains is one of the poorest matchmaking I've ever suffered through but is not what I'm discussing in particular. What I'm presenting is that the players who host custom matches are some of the most shallow and empty minded individuals that have ever graced this earth. To those who don't know, customs work where you host a match, edit the MS roster that people choose from, and then anyone can join and play. Sounds simple and should remedy bad matchmaking, right? Wrong! About 90% of the custom lobbies (among about 5-6 lobbies on a good day during peak hours) listed will be whats known as a "A WIN Rotate" game where MS costs are unrestricted, its a 1 round elimination match, and both teams are socially expected to take turns not playing the round (Whole Match) to allow the other team a guaranteed win (for the purpose of grinding the monthly missions, currency, and leveling up Mobile Suits) while match 'rotations' are normally a 5-6 minute process, meaning you have to wait every 10 minutes before its your turn to play. You might be thinking you can just AFK it and do something else while getting free progression right? Wrong! The game has this wonderful feature where you have to confirm you're MS after teams are formed but before the match actually starts, and if you don' confirm you'll get booted by the game, not the host, and have to wait until that last player slot is filled (I forgot to mention that all games, both official and custom can't actually be started unless you have a max lobby, normally 10-12 players). and after the match is said and done with, you have to manually confirm, again, the exp you gained and the rewards you may or may not have acquired (not guaranteed even with a win). My biggest quarrel with these lobbies is that they take players out of the pool, waste their time without them knowing or even caring because of 'EZ LOOT', and now you and everyone else who wants to play the game the way it was intended via custom or official matches have to wait for sometimes hours at a time just to get an actual shooter experience. In conclusion, customs could have been the cure for the worst matchmaking to exist and sometimes are, but the players in the community ruined that prospect.

This is a great game for any MS Gundam fan. It looks fantastic, you can control your MS relatively well, and you have lots of cool animations in battle. It may seem a bit clunky at first, but I liked it after a while. It makes you feel like your really piloting a massive, four story war machine that walks. The control scheme is a bit wonky from the start but you have the option to change the key bindings if you so choose. Honestly the stock control scheme isn't so bad once you get the hang of it. Despite the clunky nature of the controls, your MS are quite fast and agile ( depending on which one you choose). The MP is quite fun, when you're able to find a game. I haven't experienced bad servers per say, more like not many people playing at certain times it seems. It can take a while to find a game at times, but it's worth the wait IMO. Even single player battles are worth checking out. There isn't much in terms of single player content but it's at least replayable. You have a HUGE variety of MS's to choose from from the Guntank to the all the newer MS's ( I haven't watched the newer anime's, I'm watching them in order). You can upgrade them / customize your MS's to your hearts content. They have space battles and ground battles in which you can exit your mobile suit as your custom pilot and play boots on the ground. Over all its a great game with a bit of a tough learning curve, but not too bad. If you're willing to learn the game, it's a super fun and rewarding experience. Despite all the hate this game gets, I'd say it's worth playing and really worth giving a fair shake. If you have a decent PC and a decent graphics card this game runs consistently at 60 FPS easy on max settings ( while in battle / matches. The hub world drops FPS but not unplayable by any means with the right equipment). It isn't the most graphically intense game so it wont require much to run it smooth and crisp. I have my PC hooked up via ether net and I have experienced ZERO latency issues and no lag at all while in a match. I seriously cannot recommend checking it out enough if your a MS Gundam fan. You'll geek out in minutes of playing ( I sure did lol).

The ATC hold short issues are bad, ATC approach procedures are bad, ATC handoffs are bad, everything ATC related is bad. I always get docked points for poor airline procedures which is B.S. because it doesn't work. Firstly lets address the elephant in the room - Game or Sim? It's both actually. Eg I've spent most of my time in the career mode of MSFS 2024 and after acquiring my PPL I've been taking people up for sight seeing flights in the Cessna 172. Even though there's an element of reality to how things are done it feels like a game when flown as per the instructions. The simulator side of things is where MSFS 2024 really comes alive. I took the A320 V2 for a quick flight from YSCB to YSSY using Simbrief to import a flight plan and then, via the inbuilt flight planner, gained access to all of the required charts for each airport. By following correct procedures and utilising the included charts it's easy to forget that you're sitting in front of a PC. Sure, there are some bugs that need to be fixed but nothing game breaking for me thus far. If you're sitting on the fence go buy it. It'll only get better from here.

So everyone in the Flight Sim community has been waiting for the immensely hyped MSFS 2024. Well after almost 300 hours and some next-to-nothing update patches...I have to say I'm a bit disappointed. I, for one, was very much looking forward to Career Mode for it to give a bit more purpose to flying flights more than just scenery and the fun of setting up a flight, taking off, and then descending on an approach into an awesome looking location! Those are all still awesome to do but Career Mode gives that added sense of accomplishment and goal setting that MSFS2020 was missing. Well, unfortunately, Career Mode has so many bugs and mistakes that some missions are just more of an annoyance than enjoyable because the lack of any QA on the missions instantly kills the immersion and purpose of Career Mode altogether. If its not loading into the mission in the middle of trees or with the aircraft surrounded by buildings, people, and/or other aircraft so you can't move without hitting something, then its ATC telling you to taxi to a runway without clearance to cross the other runway which is required to get to the point they told you to go. So then you get yelled at and your overall score suffers because YOU screwed up! It really just feels like there was not enough, or any, Quality Assurance and verification on missions to make sure they worked the way they should. Then there is the whole factor about the aircraft themselves and how they, too, are all bugged and not working properly. I get it....its a new simulator and it took a bit for 2020 to be as good as it is but c'mon guys....you already knew what you were doing this time and you had 4 years to make it a killer sim! After all that being said, it is still worth getting and flying the free flights and activities! There are changes and fixes on the horizon, Im sure of it and my hope is that 2025 will bring the fixes and updates that MSFS2024 desperately needs to live up to its hype! Happy Flying! CYA!

As a sim player, its fun. I like the career mode and its features. That is something I've been looking for for a long time. As a pilot irl, its awful. Flight mechanics are wrong, speeds are wrong, power settings are wrong (75% load in the DA40 NG should get you roughly 120Kts depending on conditions, NOT 70...), the "co-pilot" will dock you points for things that are perfectly normal, but that's just how simulators are. Anyone with a pilot's license knows that sims are never as accurate as the real thing, and often are FAR from the real thing. If you want to use MSFS 2024 to learn how to fly, take it with a grain of salt. If you're using it to improve or hone your real flying skills, go to a flight school and ask to use their sims or just go fly with a CFI. But if you want to have fun and experience getting paid fake money to fly various planes around for different jobs, or even just seeing what runways the Beluga can actually take off from while at max weight, this sim is PERFECT!!! Again, its not a 1-to-1 replication of real life... DO NOT TRY TO LAND A CESSNA CARAVAN AT 180 KNOTS IN REAL LIFE!!! Use the sim for that... but it is fun to try. (side note, TURN THE TURBULENCE DOWN IF YOU WANT TO HAVE FUN!!! It is automatically set to "realistic" and its just insane updrafts and the plane attempting to tailspin itself at cruise speed)

I would recommend Flight Simulator 2024. After 4 days of being unable to log on to my X-box account and unable to play the game. The glitch was finally fixed and now I can play the game without any further problems. Although in the beginning after completing my character, picking out my plane in free flight. After I picked my departure destination and then right after I clicked my arrival destination my game crashed right to the desktop. This happened 4 times. So I then went to career mode and started my flight training and so far my game has not crashed. Although they expect perfection during my flight training. The average person just wanting to be able to fly for fun might lose interest or be frustrated enough to find another game. Flight Simulator 2024 is not an FAA certified flight training program. So expecting perfection to obtain a private pilots licence from the average person wanting to fly for fun isn't really in their best interests to encourage someone to take an interest in flying. But so far I am really impressed with what Flight Simulator 2024 has accomplished and would agree it's the best flight simulator to date. I have owned every single flight simulator that Microsoft Flight Simulator has made all the way back to 1982. So I can say with a certain degree from personal experience they have made an excellent flight simulator. My concerns after Flight Simulator 2020 was not having a working Air Traffic Control System that would give you IFR course corrections and put you right in front of the runway for landing. Especially because in Flight Simulator 2020 they just gave you GPS to the airport and wouldn't give you course corrections and line you up in front of the runway. In Flight Simulator 2020 I couldn't use the bad weather for this very reason and the traffic controller would say "Go where we talked about". Instead of IFR course corrections to line you up in front of the runway in really bad weather conditions. I understand Flight Simulator 2024 has an awesome weather system and as long as they have a working IFR Air Traffic Control System as well. Then I will be a great fan of it. So after playing 20 hours of Flight Simulator 2024 I am so far impressed. Once they get all the bugs out and things start running smooth the way they want I think everyone will agree it's the best simulator out there. Again and I can't state enough as long as they have a working Air Traffic Control System that can line you up in front of any given runway and give course corrections in bad weather it will be the greatest simulator out there. Especially in career mode which is something that I have wanted and so many other flight simulator gamers and real pilots have wanted. It's opened up a real world of possibilities and added a new dimension to the flight simulator which I am really excited about. So I have high expectations for Flight Simulator 2024. I plan to dig deep inside this sim to see if all my expectations will come to fruition. I encourage others to come in to this flight simulator with an open mind. I hope it's everything they claim it will be and I will be checking to see if it has everything I was disappointed about in Flight Simulator 2020. So for now I am recommending Flight Simulator 2024 to everyone to try.

I cannot recommend this sim as an improvement to MSFS 2020. The detail of the terrain is much better in 2024, but everything else is worse. I fly exclusively in VR and 2024 does not run as smoothly, even after weeks of tweaking and testing. The textures, clouds, sun and stars look far worse. The flight model doesn't feel as realistic. The planes seem to wander left and right on their yaw axis for no reason. Rudder control seems either too "locked in" when taxiing or you don't have any control at all. The career mode is a mess. Work hard to buy your own plane and start building your company only to find that sometimes there are no missions available at all. The economy is not well planned. Some missions don't pay enough while others are insanely lucrative. Same goes for the cost of new aircraft and maintenance. For example, a moderately bouncy landing (not a crash) in the X Cub might damage a $1200 tire along with a $40000 landing gear. I also had one instance where the X Cub was in fairly worn condition, but everything was serviceable, and it checked out fine during preflight. I lost all elevator control during a very straight and level flight, which by itself would be incredibly unlikely, but then I figured my only option would be to reroute to the nearest airport and land with only trim and throttle control, which I managed to do, but because I couldn't fly the plane and I couldn't fix the plane, the only option was to abort the mission. Things could be done much better. At this point, I have little hope that they will fix this sim and right now the fact is that MSFS 2020 is FAR better than this.
Hopefully they can fix the issues, i have no doubt they will come by with solutions and i wish them all the best. When it works it's beautiful and feels amazing.

Now a few days have passed I can say that minus the regular Crash to Desktop's I'm having the game when functional is really good, the level of detail is incredible. The career mode is still very buggy in many ways however, taxi ways are non-existent/not drive-able or the ability to respond to ATC is just sometimes not available, causing you to lose points on almost every mission through no fault of your own. The wind is also ridiculous when flying a smaller aircraft such as the Cessna but feels fine in the much larger airliners.

After the loading fiasco, everything seems as promised. Really enjoying the career mode. There is obviously some polishing left to be done; but overall I am very pleased that we have flight simulation game that is alive, well, and growing.

That said, I'm not seeing a lot of discussion on the sound, particularly the super ♥♥♥♥♥♥ text to speech ai voices. I find the lack of discussion ironic because that is a key part of immersion, which is being hailed in this version of MSFS. I'm not going to lie, I feel absolutely 0% immersion with voices on because every single syllable is so digital and fake. I can't believe that they couldn't offer Microsoft employees across the world a chance to record a few lines for a game, or better yet, offer them some pay. Phoned in lines from Crime Boss Rockay City were at least fun to laugh at, but this will make you mad you spent the minimum $70 on a game that didn't even try to do sound. That's a whole category of development that should figure into the scores reviews are providing. Wait for a sale, wait for a sound mod, wait for the next game... Just wait...

Many improvements have been made since the dismal initial launch. The game is now at least playable. Career mode is an interesting change to what we had with MSFS 2020, but still needs some tweaks to improve the experience. The sim still has not, to my knowledge, been patched to the point that you can guarantee when launching a flight your aircraft won't spawn clipped into a building, or with a giant red "ERROR" message where your pilot avatar should be sitting in the cockpit, but things are moving in the right direction. I'm looking forward to the implementation of more features in the coming months (such as the marketplace going live) to flesh out the sim and add more depth and immersion. The AI still needs some work as, for example, the voices of passengers are really monotonous and boring, especially if you're spending time doing similar missions to increase your experience in career mode. Texture and terrain loading can still be patchy and slow, especially if you're flying over dense urban areas, but once you're at higher altitudes the sim certainly looks quite impressive in it's realism. The developers have made great strides in the past couple of months. Hopefully this trend is one which will continue!
